utah.temperature: Under primarily positive 500-hPa height anomalies through much of the 6-10 day period, above normal temperatures are favored for most of the southern two-thirds of the CONUS, excluding parts of the northwestern CONUS, the Northern Tier, the northeastern CONUS, and the mid-Atlantic coast.
utah.precipitation: Above normal precipitation is favored over a large area of the CONUS from California eastward across the Central and Southern Rockies into the Central and Southern Plains, ahead of a predicted trough over the Pacific.

ne.temperature: Under primarily positive 500-hPa height anomalies through much of the 6-10 day period, above normal temperatures are favored for most of the southern two-thirds of the CONUS, excluding parts of the northwestern CONUS, the Northern Tier, the northeastern CONUS, and the mid-Atlantic coast.
ne.precipitation: Below normal precipitation is favored from the interior central Gulf Coast region northeastward across the Ohio Valley and Appalachians into the Northeast and eastern Great Lakes region, under a persistent ridge .

utah.temperature: Over the western CONUS, temperature forecasts are increasingly uncertain, as a trough and negative 500-hPa height anomalies expand into the region.
utah.precipitation: Probabilities exceed 50 percent for most of the southwestern CONUS, with enhanced moisture flow into the region ahead of a trough to the west.

ne.temperature: Above normal temperatures are favored across most of the eastern CONUS, excluding northern New England, under persistent ridging and positive 500-hPa height anomalies .
ne.precipitation: Above normal precipitation is favored across most of the CONUS, excluding near the Canadian border from Washington to Minnesota and the northeastern CONUS, consistent with the precipitation consolidation.

utah.temperature: Downstream over the CONUS, above normal temperatures are likely for much of the West, consistent with most dynamical models and the manual blend.
utah.precipitation: Above normal precipitation is slightly favored for most of the Pacific Northwest into the Northern Rockies, ahead of the amplified trough to the west.

ne.precipitation: Above normal precipitation is favored across the southern tier into the Gulf Coast region, under weak negative 500-hPa height anomalies, and northward up the East Coast into southern New England, consistent with the JMA precipitation forecast.
